recommendation_summary: Act now: replace row retrieval and in-memory object counting with a PostgreSQL COUNT(*) over unpaid invoices in the existing application, then measure latency and verify freshness before shipping this week. Optional additions: none; the reply explicitly ships no new services or topics. Unmet needs: none; it keeps request-time committed-data semantics and notes that an async projection cannot guarantee that freshness.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You require an unpaid-invoice count within one second that reflects committed invoices at request time.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, CQRS, and Redis for this count; approved budget and peer adoption do not establish a need.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint retrieves and constructs objects only to count them; the actual latency bottleneck is unmeasured.
labels.Checked myself: Only the facts you supplied; no query plan or timing evidence.

note: All four record lines come before a bounded aggregate-query recommendation that names and removes the Kafka/CQRS/Redis stack, and the reply does not claim any testing.
